The image shows a sugarcane leaf with distinct streaking patterns — alternating green and lighter/pale green/yellowish streaks running along the length of the leaf blade. The streaks are linear and parallel to the leaf veins, which is characteristic of mosaic or streak virus diseases.

Key observations:
- **Affected part**: Leaf
- **Pattern**: Linear streaks running parallel to leaf veins, alternating between darker and lighter green
- **Color**: Mosaic of green and pale/yellowish-green tones
- **Texture**: No necrosis, no lesions, no spots — purely a color variation/streaking pattern
- **No yellow margin or midrib yellowing** (ruling out Yellow Leaf)
- **No discrete oval/round spots** (ruling out Yellow_Spot, Brown_Spot)
- **No white/tan scald lesions** (ruling out Leaf_Scald)

The streaking pattern is characteristic of **Streak Mosaic** caused by Sugarcane streak mosaic virus (SCSMV), which produces fine, pale green to yellowish streaks along the leaf veins. This differs from Sugarcane Mosaic Virus (which typically shows more irregular mosaic patches rather than fine parallel streaks).
